title: AI training
subtitle: how it learns from data
facts: A model learns from many examples, each with a known right answer (or, for language models, the real next word).
For each example it makes a guess, and the guess is compared with the right answer to measure the error.
The error is used to adjust the model's internal numbers, called weights or parameters; modern models have millions to billions of them.
Repeating this over many rounds makes the guesses better. The accuracy bar is illustrative and marked as an example.
